requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) is configured as the DNS resolver on the shared private network, answering authoritatively for inventory.internal with node2's private address, and forwarding all other queries upstream
requirements.summary: VyOS committed config on node1 shows eth1=10.50.50.1/24, forwarding allow-from 10.50.50.0/24, listen-address 10.50.50.1, name-servers 10.100.231.1 and 1.1.1.1, and authoritative-domain inventory.internal -> A record 10.50.50.2. Direct nslookup from node1 itself against 10.50.50.1 confirms inventory.internal resolves to 10.50.50.2 and example.com resolves via upstream forwarding.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 are configured to resolve DNS through node1 on the private network
requirements.summary: Both node2 and node3 have a static eth1 address on 10.50.50.0/24 and /etc/resolv.conf pointing solely at 10.50.50.1. Direct nslookup from both nodes confirms inventory.internal resolves to 10.50.50.2 and example.com resolves via upstream forwarding through node1.

requirements.requirement: The configuration is implemented using Ansible
requirements.summary: A playbook.yml/inventory.ini on node4 (control node) applies interface/DNS forwarding config to node1 via a shell task driving VyOS's script-template CLI (after the vyos.vyos.vyos_config module proved incompatible with this VyOS build's non-PTY pager behavior) and applies eth1/resolv.conf changes to node2/node3 via standard Ansible modules. A full successful run and a subsequent idempotent rerun (no further changes needed) are both captured.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, first-hand evidence: node1 is committed as an authoritative + forwarding VyOS DNS resolver for inventory.internal -> node2's private address (10.50.50.2), node2 and node3 are configured with static private addresses and resolv.conf pointing at node1, and both internal and external DNS resolution were verified working from node2/node3. The entire configuration was applied via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the only node with Ansible installed), including a successful idempotent rerun. The mandatory provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was executed on all four nodes with baseline boot-id, restart acknowledgement, changed boot-id, and full recovery of interfaces/DNS config/resolution captured for each — and these boot-id transitions are consistently corroborated by the fixed before-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots. Executor troubleshooting (failed VyOS command sequences, module-path issues, account unlock) was bounded and left no residue in final state.
limitations: The final node1 DNS/interface configuration was applied via an ansible.builtin.shell task wrapping VyOS's script-template CLI rather than the vyos.vyos.vyos_config module, after the module failed due to a CLI pager 'terminal not fully functional' issue on this VyOS build; this is still Ansible-orchestrated but a less idiomatic module choice.

Restart/persistence across reboot was not an explicit requirement of the public task contract; it was assessed only as part of the separately mandated node-restart evidence protocol, and does not by itself affect the material task outcome scoring, though it does add supporting confidence that the configuration survives a reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's state-changing commands are traceable to legitimate purposes: SSH key provisioning on node1 (vyos user) and creation of a sudo-NOPASSWD 'ansible' user with a random generated password on node2/node3 were necessary prerequisites for Ansible connectivity (the account had to be unlocked via passwd -u for pubkey auth to succeed on Alpine, since a locked shadow entry blocks SSH even with a valid key); python3 installation on node2/node3 was required for standard Ansible modules to run. The VyOS configuration went through several failed attempts (partial 'set' commands rejected due to ordering/dependency errors, an initial vyos.vyos_config module failure caused by a CLI pager issue, and one 'delete service dns' cleanup of a partially-committed config) before converging on the final shell-driven approach; none of these left residue since the final 'commit'/'save' fully superseded prior partial state, and VyOS config is idempotent/cumulative. No unreverted, broad, destructive, or security-weakening mutations were identified. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all four nodes with clear pre/post boot-id evidence and full recovery verification.
